hypothesis: Jerome's Q6 asked whether the kernel can be a neural network fitted by EM and whether it overfits. On the AR(1) and phi^4 laboratories the answer was no: a 25-parameter kernel beats the MDN (E25-E31, E33, E41), but the MDN's only win came where the Gibbs class is misspecified (E36x, stride 4). E43's second laboratory, a Laplace bond on a double well outside the tilted-walk class, is the clean test of whether the neural kernel earns its parameters there, and whether the 100-parameter log-linear kernel (E43) is a better answer than the 1,516-parameter MDN.
design: The frozen E43 driver, part kernels, unmodified, at other settings: cell LAP_B_L32, arm em_mdn only, M in (128, 512, 2048), seeds 0-7 (two shards of four: e49-s0, s4), E33's EM ladder. Comparators: E43's frozen lab-B fits (site energy, tilted spline, mixture, log-linear) on the same seeds and bundles (hashes compared at read time).

predeclared_predictions.P1: At M = 2048 the MDN is below the site energy in at least 7 of 8 seeds (a state-dependent mixture can represent what a Gaussian bond cannot).
predeclared_predictions.P2: At M = 2048 the MDN is below the mixture in at least 7 of 8 seeds (E33's order).
predeclared_predictions.P3: At M = 2048 the 100-parameter log-linear kernel (E43) is below the MDN in at least 6 of 8 seeds: parsimony against the neural kernel again.
predeclared_predictions.P4: At M = 2048 at most 30% of the MDN fits select the last checkpoint (E41: the budget does not bind).

predeclared_analysis: kernels.csv (risk-selected rows) merged over the shards, paired per seed with E43's frozen lab-B rows at the same M (test-bundle hashes compared); a failed fit counts against; read by tools/make_extension_numbers.py.
provenance_note: Written after E43 and E41 were read and before any E49 cell ran. P3 is the one I am least sure of: the MDN has fifteen times the parameters but is a very different family.
resources: cluster, defq, 2 x 8 cpus, 24G, 12 h; an MDN fit took about 1 h at M = 2048 in E33 (shared nodes)
status: REGISTERED and PREDECLARED 2026-10-09; RUN on the cluster (692004, 692007: 58 and 55 min on cnode03, clean 3fed270; started 10 Oct after the maintenance window); FROZEN 2026-10-12 (hpc_E49_s0, s4; 24 em_mdn keys plus 12 lmmse_true reference keys per shard); READ: P1, P2 CONFIRMED, P3, P4 FALSIFIED

hpc_runs.smoke: the argument string run end to end at tiny settings (exit 0)

outcome.read: 2026-10-12, outputs/hpc_E49_s{0,4}/kernels.csv (risk-selected rows; 8 seeds x M in 128, 512, 2048), paired with E43's frozen lab-B fits on the same seeds (test-bundle hashes checked equal), tools/make_extension_numbers.py read_e49 as pinned.
outcome.P1: CONFIRMED. M = 2048: the MDN is below the site energy in 7 of 8 seeds; mean of per-seed ratios MDN / site energy 0.546 (the exception, seed 4, stopped by convergence at checkpoint 85 with risk 0.121).
outcome.P2: CONFIRMED. M = 2048: the MDN is below the mixture in 8 of 8 seeds (mean ratio 0.244).
outcome.P3: FALSIFIED, in the direction that favours the neural kernel. M = 2048: the 100-parameter log-linear kernel is below the MDN in only 1 of 8 seeds; the MDN is below it in 7 of 8 (mean of per-seed ratios MDN / log-linear 0.83; the pinned reading reports the inverse ratio log-linear / MDN, 1.33 as a mean of per-seed ratios). Parsimony did not win again here: on this out-of-class chain the 1,516-parameter network kernel is the best arm.
outcome.P4: FALSIFIED as registered (reading rule: at_cap == 1 in more than 30% of fits): 5 of 8 at M = 2048 (1 of 8 at M = 512, 0 of 8 at M = 128). One of the five is seed 4, which stopped by convergence at checkpoint 85 and is flagged only because it is the last saved one; four fits (seeds 0, 1, 5, 6) selected the last checkpoint, 1200, of E33's EM ladder. E49 used E33's ladder, not E41's extended one, so the MDN risks at M = 2048 are upper bounds and more budget can only widen its lead.
outcome.tables: Seed-mean risk on LAP_B_L32 (linear floor 0.2434 at every M): M = 128 / 512 / 2048: MDN 0.1085 / 0.0664 / 0.0563; log-linear 0.1209 / 0.0796 / 0.0675; site energy 0.1090 / 0.1057 / 0.1029; tilted spline 0.1137 / 0.1079 / 0.1041; mixture 0.2377 / 0.2334 / 0.2305. MDN below the site energy in 5, 8, 7 of 8 seeds, below the log-linear in 6, 8, 7 of 8, below the spline in 5, 8, 7 of 8, below the mixture in 8, 8, 8 of 8, at M = 128, 512, 2048.
outcome.reading: The crossover E43 reported for the unrestricted kernel on this chain (lab B) (it overtakes the Gaussian-bond families between M = 128 and 512) happens at the same place for the neural kernel, and the neural kernel then keeps its lead over the unrestricted one: at M = 2048 it has 1.8 times lower risk than the site energy (0.0563 against 0.1029) and 17% lower than the log-linear kernel. Together with E48 (stride 4, clean data) this answers Jerome's question 'does the neural kernel ever earn its parameters?': yes, where the physics is outside the Gibbs class it earns them, by a factor of 1.8 to 2.5 against the best Gaussian-bond kernel in both measured settings (E48, stride 4: the MDN's risk is 0.40 times the site energy's; E49, M = 2048: 0.55 times); where the class is correct (the phi^4 field itself) it does not (E33, E41). Caveats: one constructed chain (Laplace bond on a double well, calibrated to the base cell's correlation and kurtosis), eight seeds, and both the MDN (4 of 8 at its last checkpoint) and the log-linear kernel (23 of 24 lab-B fits at its iteration cap, E43) were budget-limited; the ranking MDN < log-linear could change with budget on either side.
